questions.stem: Why do roots need to use active transport to absorb mineral ions from the soil?

options.text: Because mineral ions are too large to cross cell membranes by diffusion
Because the concentration of minerals is usually higher inside the root than in the soil
Because minerals can only dissolve in water at high temperatures
Because minerals must first be converted to sugars before absorption

questions.explanation: Mineral ions are usually present in the soil at a lower concentration than inside the root cells. This means they must be absorbed against their concentration gradient, which requires active transport using energy from respiration.
